question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` continue accepting numerically equivalent plus-prefixed and zero-padded decimal spellings, or become a canonical-text-only CLI contract?
rationale: Current behavior accepts these spellings and the docs do not promise canonical textual syntax, so rejecting them is an intentional compatibility policy choice that source inspection cannot authorize.

options.title: Keep equivalent spellings accepted
options.body: Preserve the existing normalization and close or narrow this PR unless concrete user harm from these aliases is demonstrated.

options.title: Adopt canonical-only input
options.body: Explicitly approve the compatibility break, document it, and require real CLI before/after/control proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep equivalent spellings accepted
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing normalization and close or narrow this PR unless concrete user harm from these aliases is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: This requires repository-level CLI compatibility direction rather than further mechanical implementation work.
